subject: Training usage & retention commitments — Acme DPA questions
messages:
From: Claire Hammond <claire@acmecorp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Corp Security <security@acmecorp.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Training usage assurances and retention details

Hi Jordan,

We're reviewing Redwood for a pilot and legal/security asked for two quick clarifications before we proceed:

1) Training: Does Redwood use customer-provided content (API payloads, uploaded files, prompts, logs) to train or fine-tune any models, or for model improvement by default? If so, under what conditions?

2) Retention & deletion: What data retention windows apply to request payloads, request/response logs, and derived telemetry? How quickly can data be deleted on request, and what happens to backups and logs?

Please include any standard contract language you can provide or a pointer to the DPA with your suggested redlines.

Thanks — Claire
Claire Hammond
Head of Platform Security, Acme Corp
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Claire Hammond <claire@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Training usage assurances and retention details

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear questions. High-level answers up front, followed by attachments and next steps.

TL;DR:
- Training: We do not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or improve Redwood public models without explicit, written customer consent.
- Retention: Default short-term logs are retained for troubleshooting and fraud detection; longer-term analytics are aggregated. We support contract-level retention customization and will accept DPA redlines for enterprise accounts.

Details:
- Training / Model updates:
  - Hosted API: Customer content is not included in model training datasets or weight updates. We may retain anonymized telemetry (e.g., latency/error rates, token length distributions) for service health and capacity planning; that telemetry is not reversible to customer content.
  - Dedicated & Private deployments: No customer data is used to train our models. For Private (on-prem/VPC) deployments, Redwood does not access customer data by default.

- Retention & deletion:
  - Request payloads / responses: default retention 30 days for direct troubleshooting; can be shortened via contract.
  - Debug logs / traces: short-lived by default (30–90 days) depending on log type; audit logs used for billing/forensics kept longer (configurable).
  - Deletion on request: standard process is a verified delete request → data purged from primary stores within 72 hours; secondary backups and snapshots follow the documented purge workflow (deletion tombstones applied; full removal by next backup cycle).

Attached: SOC2-Summary.pdf (high-level assurance) and our proposed DPA redline (DPA-redline.docx).

If you’d like, I can loop in our legal and security teams for any contract-level language changes. Would a short call tomorrow work to walk through the DPA?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Training usage assurances and retention details

Hi Claire — Naomi (Legal) here, following up with the contract framing Jordan mentioned. Reposting the key proposed DPA language we typically offer to enterprise customers:

Proposed contract snippet (for review):
"Redwood will not use Customer Content to train, improve, or benchmark any models (including internal models used for Redwood services) or to generate derivative models, except where (i) Customer provides prior written consent for specific usage, or (ii) Customer explicitly uploads data to a model-training pipeline as part of a paid professional services engagement.
Redwood may collect aggregated and de-identified service telemetry necessary for operational metrics; such telemetry will not contain Customer Content and will not be used to identify Customer or end-users."

Retention mechanics we recommend in the DPA redline:
- Default request data TTL: 30 days (shorter TTLs available by agreement).
- Audit/billing logs: retained 365 days (can be reduced).
- Deletion SLA: verified delete requests executed within 72 hours for primary data stores; backups removed according to backup lifecycle (typically within 30 days from request, with exceptions documented).

If Acme needs stricter timelines (e.g., 7-day backup purge), we can include that as a mark in the DPA and document the operational steps.

I'll also note we attach our SOC 2 summary for quick review; full SOC 2 report can be shared under NDA.

Naomi Feldman
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Training usage assurances and retention details — technical clarifications

Hi Claire — quick technical follow-up on Naomi/Jordan's notes to clarify how data flows and retention map to our infrastructure:

- No training on customer content:
  - Our production model weights are static for hosted endpoints; we do not run back-propagation or persistent gradient accumulation using customer payloads. Any offline research datasets are segregated and do not ingest live customer payloads.

- Caching & KV stores:
  - Prefix/KV caches used for request acceleration are ephemeral by design. Default TTLs are in-memory or short-lived persistent caches (minutes to hours) and are purged on session termination. Customers on Dedicated can opt into persistent caching, which we document in the config and in the DPA.

- Logs, backups, and snapshots:
  - Primary request/response storage: encrypted at rest (AES-256) and deleted per TTL or verified delete.
  - Backups & snapshots: encrypted and retained per backup policy. On a verified deletion request we mark data for purge (tombstone) and exclude it from restores; final removal occurs at next backup cycle (we document cycles in the DPA).
  - Immutable audit logs used for security investigations are retained per contract; access is restricted and logged.

- Telemetry for product improvement:
  - We collect aggregated metrics (error rates, latency histograms, token distribution). These metrics are aggregated and cannot be used to reconstruct Customer Content.

If helpful, I can prepare a short architecture diagram showing data flows (request → runtime → cache → logs → retention lifecycle). Happy to join a call with your security team.

— Dev Patel
